results.summary_before: This Verilog design monitors three input signals and asserts an alarm output when all three are active within the same time window of about six seconds at 100 MHz. The three sensor inputs are on the lower input pins and the single response output is on the first output pin. External sensors, buttons or similar sources drive the inputs, and the output can be connected to an LED, display or sounder. The documentation is very short and gives no detail on the timing logic or any test results.

results.summary_before: Quickscope is a small logic analyzer that samples eight input pins and the bidirectional pins and streams the captured values over UART. It triggers when ui[0] goes high and sends data at 115200 baud on uo[0], where a host client converts it into a VCD file viewable in Surfer. Testing requires connecting a UART adapter and the signals to be analyzed. The documentation refers to an external blog post for details, so the on-chip implementation is not described in the project text.

No external hardware is required, but the filter coefficients and exact behavior are not documented.

results.summary_before: This design implements a digital flight control mixer for a delta wing aircraft, processing control inputs and generating PWM signals for elevon and rudder actuators. It uses a command-based protocol on the 8-bit input bus to load control registers, and outputs time-multiplexed actuator commands on the 8-bit output bus, with a 3-bit channel tag and 5-bit PWM value. The design is fully digital and does not require external hardware to operate, but for practical use, the output can be connected to a microcontroller or servo drivers. The documentation describes the command protocol and output format, but does not provide details on the stabilization logic or testing procedures.

results.summary_before: This design provides a streaming byte-fed accumulator generated from an MLIR for-loop pattern, implementing a specialized S3FDP accumulator for bfloat16 multiplication and addition. It is part of a toolflow that detects loop patterns and emits optimized arithmetic circuits instead of generic floating-point datapaths. The design has a byte-wide input and output interface and requires no external hardware. It is notable for being generated automatically from MLIR and for its use of the Kulisch accumulator architecture.
